summary: This mishnah lists who gets the punishment of burning (certain forbidden relationships) and who gets the sword (a murderer and the people of an ir hanidachas). It also teaches when someone counts as a murderer.

chunks.en: These are the ones who are burned:
chunks.st: And these are the transgressors who are burned
chunks.stMore: in the implementation of the court-imposed death penalty:

chunks.en: one who sins with a woman and her daughter,
chunks.st: One who engaged in intercourse with a woman and her daughter,

chunks.en: and a Kohen's daughter who did a forbidden sin.
chunks.st: and one who is the daughter of a priest and who committed adultery.

chunks.en: Under "a woman and her daughter" are included:
chunks.st: Included in the category of the prohibition of engaging in intercourse with a woman and her daughter and the resulting execution by burning, there are:

chunks.en: his daughter, his daughter's daughter, his son's daughter,
chunks.st: His daughter, and the daughter of his daughter, and the daughter of his son.
chunks.stMore: Likewise, the following are also included in this category: Intercourse with

chunks.he: וּבַת אִשְׁתּוֹ, וּבַת בִּתָּהּ, וּבַת בְּנָהּ,
chunks.en: his wife's daughter, her daughter's daughter, her son's daughter,
chunks.st: the daughter of his wife, even though she is not his daughter, and the daughter of her daughter, and the daughter of her son,

chunks.en: his mother-in-law, his mother-in-law's mother, and his father-in-law's mother.
chunks.st: as well as intercourse with his mother-in-law, and the mother of his mother-in-law, and the mother of his father-in-law.
chunks.stMore: The prohibition and punishment apply both in cases where a man marries a woman and then engages in intercourse with her daughter, and in cases where a man marries a woman and then engages in intercourse with her mother.

chunks.en: And these are the ones killed by the sword:
chunks.st: And these are the transgressors who are killed
chunks.stMore: by decapitation in the implementation of the court-imposed death penalty:

chunks.en: the murderer, and the people of an ir hanidachas.
chunks.st: The murderer; and the residents of an idolatrous city, all of whom engaged in idol worship.

words.note: A city where everyone served idols.

chunks.he: רוֹצֵחַ שֶׁהִכָּה אֶת רֵעֵהוּ בְאֶבֶן אוֹ בְבַרְזֶל,
chunks.en: A murderer who hit his friend with a stone or with iron,
chunks.st: The mishna elaborates: In the case of a murderer who struck another with a stone or with iron,

chunks.en: or held him down in the water
chunks.st: or held him in the water

chunks.en: or in the fire,
chunks.st: or in the fire, and

chunks.en: and he could not get out of there,
chunks.st: the victim could not extricate himself from there

chunks.en: and he died, is chayav.
chunks.st: and he died,the murderer is liable to be executed.

chunks.he: דְּחָפוֹ לְתוֹךְ הַמַּיִם אוֹ לְתוֹךְ הָאוּר
chunks.en: If he pushed him into the water or into the fire,
chunks.st: If one pushed another into the water or into the fire and

chunks.en: and he could have gotten out of there,
chunks.st: that person could have extricated himself from there

chunks.en: and he died, he is patur.
chunks.st: but failed to do so, and he died, the one who pushed him is exempt
chunks.stMore: from punishment by a court, as he caused the death but did not actually kill the victim.

chunks.en: If he sent a dog after him,
chunks.st: For the same reason, if one set a dog against another and the dog killed him,

chunks.en: or sent a snake after him, he is patur.
chunks.st: or if one set a snake against another and the snake killed him, the one who set the dog or the snake is exempt from punishment.

chunks.en: If he made the snake bite him,
chunks.st: If he imbedded the snake’s fangs into another and caused the snake to bite him and kill him,

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says he is chayav,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda deems him liable to be executed, as he is a murderer,

chunks.en: and the Sages say he is patur.
chunks.st: and the Rabbis exempt
chunks.stMore: him, as they maintain that he indirectly caused the individual’s death.

chunks.en: One who hits his friend,
chunks.st: In the case of one who strikes another,

chunks.en: whether with a stone or with a fist,
chunks.st: whether he does so with a stone or with his fist,

chunks.en: and they thought he would die,
chunks.st: and the doctors assessed his condition, estimating that it would lead to death,

chunks.en: and he got better than he was,
chunks.st: and then his condition eased from what it was,
chunks.stMore: and the doctors revised their prognosis and predicted that he would live,

chunks.en: and after that he got worse and died, he is chayav.
chunks.st: and thereafter his condition worsened and he died, the assailant is liable to be executed as a murderer.

chunks.en: Rabbi Nechemyah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Neḥemya says:

chunks.en: he is patur, because there is a reason to think so.
chunks.explain: Something else may have made him die.
chunks.st: He is exempt, as there is a basis for the matter
chunks.stMore: of assuming that he is not liable. Since the victim’s condition eased in the interim, a cause other than the blow struck by the assailant ultimately caused his death.

summary: A person is only punished as a murderer if he meant to kill this kind of person, and his blow was strong enough to kill where it landed. The mishnah gives many cases where his plan and what happened do not match.

chunks.en: If he meant to kill an animal
chunks.st: If one intended to kill an animal,

chunks.en: and killed a person,
chunks.st: and he killed a person standing adjacent to it,

chunks.en: or meant to kill a non-Jew and killed a Jew,
chunks.st: or if he intended to kill a gentile, for whose murder he is not liable to be executed in court, and he killed a Jew,

chunks.en: or a baby who could not live and killed one who could live, he is patur.
chunks.st: or if he intended to kill non-viable newborns, for whose murder one is not liable, and he killed a viable person, the assailant is exempt
chunks.stMore: from execution, since his intent was to kill one for whose murder he is not liable.

chunks.en: If he meant to hit him on his waist,
chunks.st: If one intended to strike another on his loins,

chunks.he: וְלֹא הָיָה בָהּ כְּדֵי לְהָמִית עַל מָתְנָיו
chunks.en: and it was not strong enough to kill on his waist,
chunks.st: and the blow was not powerful enough to kill him if it were to land on his loins,

chunks.en: but it landed on his heart,
chunks.st: but instead the blow landed on his chest over the victim’s heart,

chunks.he: וְהָיָה בָהּ כְּדֵי לְהָמִית עַל לִבּוֹ,
chunks.en: and it was strong enough to kill on his heart,
chunks.st: and it was powerful enough to kill him when it landed on his chest over his heart,

chunks.en: and he died, he is patur.
chunks.st: and the victim died as a result of the blow, the assailant is exempt
chunks.stMore: from execution, as he did not intend to strike the victim a blow that would cause his death.

chunks.en: If he meant to hit him on his heart,
chunks.st: If he intended to strike him on his chest over his heart

chunks.he: וְהָיָה בָהּ כְּדֵי לְהָמִית עַל לִבּוֹ
chunks.en: and it was strong enough to kill on his heart,
chunks.st: and the blow was powerful enough to kill him were it to land on his chest over his heart,

chunks.en: but it landed on his waist,
chunks.st: and instead the blow landed on his loins,

chunks.he: וְלֹא הָיָה בָהּ כְּדֵי לְהָמִית עַל מָתְנָיו,
chunks.en: and it was not strong enough to kill on his waist,
chunks.st: and it was not powerful enough to kill him when it landed on his loins,

chunks.en: and he died, he is patur.
chunks.st: and nevertheless the victim died, the assailant is exempt.
chunks.stMore: Although the assailant intended to kill the victim, the blow was not powerful enough to kill. Ostensibly, his death was not a result of the blow.

chunks.en: If he meant to hit a big person,
chunks.st: If one intended to kill an adult

chunks.he: וְלֹא הָיָה בָהּ כְּדֵי לְהָמִית הַגָּדוֹל
chunks.en: and it was not strong enough to kill the big one,
chunks.st: and the blow was not powerful enough to kill the adult,

chunks.en: but it landed on a small child,
chunks.st: and instead the blow landed on a minor,

chunks.he: וְהָיָה בָהּ כְּדֵי לְהָמִית אֶת הַקָּטָן,
chunks.en: and it was strong enough to kill the small one,
chunks.st: and the blow was powerful enough to kill the minor

chunks.en: and he died, he is patur.
chunks.st: and the minor died, the assailant is exempt.

chunks.en: If he meant to hit a small child,
chunks.st: If one intended to kill a minor

chunks.he: וְהָיָה בָהּ כְּדֵי לְהָמִית אֶת הַקָּטָן
chunks.en: and it was strong enough to kill the small one,
chunks.st: and the blow was powerful enough to kill a minor,

chunks.en: but it landed on a big person,
chunks.st: and the blow landed on an adult

chunks.he: וְלֹא הָיָה בָהּ כְּדֵי לְהָמִית אֶת הַגָּדוֹל,
chunks.en: and it was not strong enough to kill the big one,
chunks.st: and the blow was not powerful enough to kill the adult,

chunks.en: and he died, he is patur.
chunks.st: and nevertheless, the adult died, the assailant is exempt.

chunks.en: But if he meant to hit him on his waist,
chunks.st: But if one intended to strike another on his loins,

chunks.he: וְהָיָה בָהּ כְּדֵי לְהָמִית עַל מָתְנָיו
chunks.en: and it was strong enough to kill on his waist,
chunks.st: and the blow was powerful enough to kill him were it to land on his loins,

chunks.en: and it landed on his heart,
chunks.st: and instead the blow landed on his chest over his heart,

chunks.en: and he died, he is chayav.
chunks.st: and he died, the assailant is liable,
chunks.stMore: since in any event, his intent was to kill the victim and the blow was powerful enough to kill him wherever it struck him.

chunks.en: If he meant to hit a big person,
chunks.st: If one intended to strike an adult

chunks.he: וְהָיָה בָהּ כְּדֵי לְהָמִית אֶת הַגָּדוֹל
chunks.en: and it was strong enough to kill the big one,
chunks.st: and the blow was powerful enough to kill the adult,

chunks.en: and it landed on a small child,
chunks.st: and the blow landed on a minor

chunks.en: and he died, he is chayav.
chunks.st: and he died, the assailant is liable.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: even if he meant to kill this one
chunks.st: Even if one intended to kill this one

chunks.en: and killed that one, he is patur.
chunks.st: and he killed that one, although he would be liable for killing either, he is exempt,
chunks.stMore: because one is executed only if his action completely corresponded with his intent.

summary: What happens if we cannot tell who is the murderer, or who got which punishment? Rabbi Shimon and the Sages argue about which punishment is more severe, burning or stoning.

chunks.en: A murderer who got mixed up with other people,
chunks.st: With regard to a murderer who was intermingled with others
chunks.stMore: and it is not possible to identify the murderer,

chunks.en: all of them are patur.
chunks.st: all of them are exempt from liability to be executed.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: they put them in a locked room.
chunks.st: The court gathers them into the vaulted chamber [lakippa] where they will eventually die.

chunks.he: כָּל חַיָּבֵי מִיתוֹת שֶׁנִּתְעָרְבוּ זֶה בָזֶה,
chunks.en: All those who must get a death penalty who got mixed up with each other
chunks.st: With regard to all those liable to be executed with different court-imposed death penalties who became intermingled with each other
chunks.stMore: and it cannot be determined which individual was sentenced to which death,

chunks.en: get the easiest punishment.
chunks.st: they are all sentenced to the most lenient
chunks.stMore: form of execution to which any of them was sentenced.

chunks.en: Those who should be stoned mixed with those who should be burned:
chunks.st: In a case where those who are liable to be stoned were intermingled with those who are liable to be burned,

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: they all get stoning,
chunks.st: They are all sentenced to be executed by stoning,

chunks.en: because burning is more severe.
chunks.st: as burning is a more severe form of execution than stoning.

chunks.en: And the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: they all get burning,
chunks.st: They are all sentenced to be executed by burning,

chunks.en: because stoning is more severe.
chunks.st: as stoning is a more severe form of execution than burning.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon said to them,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon said to the Rabbis:

chunks.en: "If burning were not more severe,
chunks.st: If burning were not more severe than stoning,

chunks.en: it would not have been given to a Kohen's daughter who sinned."
chunks.st: it would not have been administered to a priest’s daughter who committed adultery.
chunks.stMore: A betrothed daughter of an Israelite who committed adultery is executed by stoning. If burning were not a more severe form of execution than stoning, it would not have been administered to the daughter of a priest who committed adultery, who would presumably receive a more severe punishment.

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: The Rabbis said to Rabbi Shimon:

chunks.en: "If stoning were not more severe,
chunks.st: If stoning were not more severe than burning

chunks.he: לֹא נִתְּנָה לַמְגַדֵּף וְלָעוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.
chunks.en: it would not have been given to one who curses Hashem and to one who serves idols."
chunks.st: it would not have been the death penalty administered to a blasphemer and to an idol worshipper,
chunks.stMore: as their actions violate the very core of the Jewish faith.

words.en: to the one who curses Hashem
and to the one who serves

chunks.en: If those killed by the sword were mixed with those who are choked,
chunks.st: There is a parallel dispute: In a case where those who are liable to be killed by beheading were intermingled with those who are liable to be strangled,

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says, by the sword.
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says: They are all sentenced to be beheaded with a sword,
chunks.stMore: as strangulation is a more severe form of execution than beheading.

chunks.en: And the Sages say, by choking.
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say: They are all sentenced to be executed by strangulation,
chunks.stMore: as beheading is a more severe form of execution than strangulation.

summary: If a person must get two different death penalties, he gets the more severe one. Rabbi Yosei says it depends on which sin was first.

chunks.he: מִי שֶׁנִּתְחַיֵּב בִּשְׁתֵּי מִיתוֹת בֵּית דִּין,
chunks.en: One who must get two death penalties of the court
chunks.st: One who is liable to be executed with two different court-imposed death
chunks.stMore: penalties, as he violated two different capital transgressions,

chunks.en: is judged with the more severe one.
chunks.st: is sentenced to the more severe form of execution.

chunks.he: עָבַר עֲבֵרָה שֶׁנִּתְחַיֵּב בָּהּ שְׁתֵּי מִיתוֹת,
chunks.en: If he did one sin that made him chayav two death penalties,
chunks.st: If one violated one transgression for which he is liable to receive two death
chunks.stMore: penalties, e.g., if one engaged in intercourse with his mother-in-law, who is also a married woman,

chunks.en: he is judged with the more severe one.
chunks.st: he is sentenced to the more severe form of execution.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: he is judged by the first reason that came upon him.
chunks.st: He is sentenced to the form of execution that he is liable to receive due to the first relationship that came upon him,
chunks.stMore: i.e., if she was his mother-in-law before she was married, he is executed by burning; if she was married before she was his mother-in-law, he is punished by strangulation.

summary: Some people who keep sinning, or whom the court cannot punish in the regular way, are put in a locked room by the court.

chunks.en: One who got lashes and did the same sin again,
chunks.st: One who was flogged for violating a prohibition and then repeated
chunks.stMore: the violation and was flogged again assumes the status of a forewarned transgressor.

chunks.en: the court puts him in a locked room
chunks.st: The court places him into the vaulted chamber [lakippa]

chunks.en: and feeds him barley,
chunks.st: and feeds him barley bread

chunks.en: until he dies from it.
chunks.st: until his belly ruptures due to the low-quality food, and he dies.

chunks.en: One who killed a person without witnesses
chunks.st: With regard to one who kills a person not in the presence of witnesses and it is impossible to judge him in court,

chunks.en: is put in a locked room
chunks.st: the court places him into a vaulted chamber

chunks.he: וּמַאֲכִילִין אוֹתוֹ לֶחֶם צַר וּמַיִם לָחַץ:
chunks.en: and given only a little bread and a little water.
chunks.st: and feeds him sparing bread and scant water (see Isaiah 30:20).

summary: For a few terrible sins, zealous people may punish the sinner themselves. A Kohen who served in the Beis HaMikdash while tamei was taken out by the young Kohanim.

chunks.en: One who steals the kasva,
chunks.st: With regard to one who steals a kasva,

words.note: A holy vessel of the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: one who curses using witchcraft,
chunks.st: and one who curses with a sorcerer,

chunks.en: and one who sins with a non-Jewish woman,
chunks.st: and one who engages in intercourse with an Aramean woman,

words.en: and the one who lives with

chunks.en: zealous people may strike him.
chunks.explain: People with great zeal for Hashem's honor.
chunks.st: zealots strike him
chunks.stMore: and kill him. Although the Torah does not say that one who performs one of these actions is liable to be executed, it is permitted for anyone who zealously takes the vengeance of the Lord to do so.

chunks.en: A Kohen who served while he was tamei,
chunks.st: In the case of a priest who performed the Temple service in a state of ritual impurity,

chunks.he: אֵין אֶחָיו הַכֹּהֲנִים מְבִיאִין אוֹתוֹ לְבֵית דִּין,
chunks.en: his brothers the Kohanim do not bring him to court,
chunks.st: his priestly brethren do not bring him to court for judgment;

chunks.he: אֶלָּא פִרְחֵי כְהֻנָּה מוֹצִיאִין אוֹתוֹ חוּץ לָעֲזָרָה
chunks.en: but the young Kohanim take him out of the Azarah
chunks.st: rather, the young men of the priesthood remove him from the Temple courtyard

words.note: The courtyard of the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: and hit his head with pieces of wood.
chunks.st: and pierce his skull with pieces of wood.

chunks.en: One who is not a Kohen who served in the Mikdash:
chunks.st: In the case of a non-priest who performed the service in the Temple,

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says, by choking.
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says: His execution is by strangulation,

chunks.en: And the Sages say, by the hands of Heaven.
chunks.explain: Hashem punishes him, not the court.
chunks.st: and the Rabbis say: He is not executed with a court-imposed death penalty; rather, he is liable to receive death at the hand of Heaven.
